title: Ordinary immersion pullback agrees with quotient-tower completed pullback
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, with $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $u:Y\to X$ be a locally closed immersion of schemes, meaning a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. On $T=X,Y$ put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the canonical coefficient isomorphism $u^{-1}B_X\cong B_Y$ and finite projection identifications [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Ordinary $Lu^*$ is pullback of modules over these ring sheaves; completed $Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ and its comparison $Lu^*K\to Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ are the strict quotient-tower construction of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

For every derived-complete $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-derived-complete, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] this specified comparison is an isomorphism. Ordinary $Lu^*=u^*$ is exact, preserves derived completeness, and has canonical finite-reduction comparisons $u^*(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X)\cong(u^*K)\otimes^L_{B_Y}(A_n)_Y$ in $D((A_n)_Y)$. These identifications respect quotient transitions, the completion unit and all finite projection maps, including successive quotients. The derived-limit comparison here is the map of strict-tower Roos models induced by the exact, countable-product-preserving inverse image, rather than a choice of a map between unrelated cones. If $K$ belongs to the integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], so does $u^*K$, with the same uniform cohomological interval for its reductions.

proof.text: The unchanged strictIso construction uses the actual completed transport and completion reflector; its finite projection equations use the normalized augmentation-unit theorem. Immersion inverse image preserves products, and the strict Roos comparison and exact-adjoint tower models, with normalized resolution uniqueness, give the original roosRlim_exists proof. These constructions remain in this module. rlimComparison_roos retains its original named hole, including the normalized mate equation. Its first clause gives invertibility on represented complexes. For the final theorem regard rlimComparison as the natural transformation supplied by mateEquiv. Naturality along a derived representative isomorphism transfers invertibility to every derived tower.

Uniqueness on quotient representatives and finite projections identifies completedRingIso with purCoefficientIso. The completeness-transport theorem identifies both detailed completeness predicates with intrinsic completeness in the original presentation.

Intrinsic completeness makes the source quotient-tower completion unit invertible. ordinaryToCompleted_eq factors ordinary-to-completed pullback as inverse image of that unit followed by the invertible derived-limit mate. strictIso gives invertibility of the actual strict unit. The unit-compatible actual/intrinsic completed-pullback comparison and closure under isomorphism imply completeness of ordinary pullback. Transport it back to the detailed coefficient category.

Retain the source uniform interval a,b. Apply the finite-reduction theorem at each n with that interval, and combine it with completeness to obtain integral constructibility. Apply the finite theorem again with the separately supplied r,s to retain that exact bound. Finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation are existing ordinary pullback instances; products follow from immersion limit preservation.
